newsitem.title: KENYA: Offloading investors drag Nairobi bourse index.
newsitem.headline: Offloading investors drag Nairobi bourse index.

text.p: Offloading investors dragged down the Nairobi Stock Exchange 20-share index on Tuesday, maintaining an overall bearish sentiment, bourse officials said.
The index shed 7.49 points to stand at 3373.72. Turnover was posted at 36.600 million shillings on 694,414 shares compared to 23.298 million shillings on 335,229 shares.

"Anybody who came into the market in December is getting out," a broker told Reuters, adding that the prevailing low prices at the exchange would persist for some time because of a lack of buying interest.

"This is a normal market cycle. Prices will be low now that most companies have announced, and will ease further until all companies trading with dividend close their books sometime in May," another broker said.
Bourse officials said activity was dominated by retailers.
Kenya Power & Lighting lost 6.0 shillings to 116, while Kenya Commercial Bank eased to 91 from 93.
Sasini Tea & Coffee, the biggest lot traded on Tuesday, supported turnover after changing 200,000 shares at a reserve price of 80 from 75 on the three-day special board.
Lonrho Motors closed the maximum 15 percent spread allowed in a day's trading on a share to close at 189 from 164.
Under NSE rules, a share cannot close below or above a maximum 15 percent spread on the previous day's closing price.
Brokers said there was increased demand for the motor share driven by an announcement of a two shares for every one held bonus issue this month.
Rea Vipingo eased to 9.75 from 10 while Standard Chartered Bank closed at 46.50 from 47.
Unga Group was unchanged at 110 while Total Kenya edged to close at 60 from 59.50.
